messages:
sam: Quick sync — we need a lightweight playbook for sequencing the next model wave (orca2, mixtral, openllama-130B-v2). GreenFin and ClearDocs are pushing orca2 first. Infra cost + Dedicated capacity constraints are real though. Thoughts on prioritization and launch gates?

maria: +1 to a playbook. Can we standardize on a 4-point gating checklist and a simple RICE sheet for tradeoffs? We should capture customer urgency separately from long-term impact.

ajay: For model-onboarding I care about: perf SLOs (p50/p95), memory floor (int8/4-bit quant), and KV cache behavior for chat. If quantization path isn't solid, some models will be too expensive to serve.

kevin: Dedicated pools have ~20% spare capacity this month but that drops if two customers go live. Autoscale helps, but network egress & region placement matter. Cost delta between mixtral and orca2 is non-trivial on A100s.

lia: Customer asks: GreenFin wants orca2 for domain-tuned summarization (high priority). ClearDocs asked for mixtral for table parsing. Both say timeline = 4–6 weeks. We should encode those as "customer impact" not just tickets.

maria: Proposed gating checklist (short):
1) Perf: passes our latency/throughput smoke tests (p95 <= 700ms for chat baseline)
2) Cost: expected unit cost delta <= 20% vs baseline or clear mitigation (quantization)
3) Compatibility: runs in Dedicated + Redwood Private with KC caching
4) Eval quality: no regression on our prompt suite (>95% quality baseline for key prompts)

sam: Love that. Can we put a tiny RICE table in-line to make decisions deterministic? Example:
```
Model       Reach  Impact  Confidence  Effort  RICE_score
orca2       8      8       0.7         4       (8*8*0.7)/4 = 11.2
mixtral     5      6       0.6         3       = 6.0
ol-130b-v2  3      7       0.5         6       = 1.75
```
(Reach = # customers + internal use, Impact = business value, Effort = relative engineering work)

ajay: Quick note: RICE is fine but we must sanity-check effort vs unknowns (quantization, kernel availability). Put a binary "quant-ready" flag so we don't over-credit models that seem cheap but need new kernels.

kevin: Also add a deployment sequencing rule: "Critical customers on Dedicated get priority if their commitment covers the runway". Means GreenFin's contract could push orca2 ahead even if RICE similar.

maria: Agreed. Proposed decision flow: RICE -> quant-ready check -> gating checklist -> customer commit override (documented and timeboxed). If override used, require a mitigation plan (e.g., temporary rates, fallback model).

lia: For handoff to solutions eng: include a one-pager checklist for customers that lists expected SLA, cost delta, and any feature gaps (tools/structured output). Keeps expectations clear.

sam: Could we capture a minimal rollout plan template? Suggest: canary (5% traffic, single region) -> monitor cost/quality 72h -> expand to 25% -> full rollout. Add automatic fallback to baseline model on errors.

product-bot: Reminder: add model entry to "onboarding tracker" and tag "quant-awaiting" if needed. Link: https://go/redwood/model-onboard-tracker

maria: OK, action items: 1) I'll make a tiny Google sheet with RICE + quant-ready + gating columns. 2) Ajay/kevin: quick feasibility call tomorrow to vet kernels & capacity. 3) Lia: collect customer commitment notes. 4) Sam: draft rollout template and one-pager.

sam: Thanks — I'll seed the sheet now and ping people. If nobody objects, we'll use this for orca2 decision by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

ajay: noted. Will bring preliminary perf numbers to tomorrow's call.

kevin: I'll check Dedicated capacity forecasts and share worst-case cost delta.

lia: I'll nudge GreenFin for a short note confirming timeline.

sam: wrapping — small, deterministic process, RICE + quant gate + customer override with mitigation. Should keep debates short and decisions trackable.

maria: +1. If we can make the sheet one-click to turn into a rollout ticket it saves ops time.

sam: good point. product-bot, can we auto-create a ticket when RICE row is marked "approved"?

product-bot: yes — create an issue template link when approved.

lia: thanks everyone :)
